narrative.overview: Atlas Travel frames travel planning as a calm, high-confidence operations surface. Near-black space, local satellite geography, and restrained cyan trajectory lines make the physical route tangible without presenting a real booking system. The visual drama belongs to the interactive Earth. Surrounding information remains compact, factual, and visibly provisional so later traditional and AI-assisted flows can occupy the same shell.
keyCharacteristics: A real-geography 3D globe is the primary workspace object.
Cyan signals active spatial context; amber marks route endpoints.
Dense but quiet panels support, rather than compete with, the globe.

rules.name: The Sparse Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan is an operational signal, not a decorative fill; reserve it for the route, interactive controls, and essential status.

rules.name: The Globe-First Rule
rules.body: Never place a dense data view where it obscures the globe’s route or its direct manipulation controls.

dos: Do keep geographic rendering real while explicitly labeling routes and planning content as illustrative.
Do reserve the right rail for evolving planning or assistant content without displacing the globe.
Do use cyan and amber with intention, preserving contrast on dark surfaces.
donts: Don't imply bookings, suppliers, map traffic, or travel data are real.
Don't turn supporting panels into bright competing focal points.
Don't make the assistant state appear active before T5 implements its behavior.
